title: South Park slams ICE in parody ad featured in latest episode - NewsBreak
text: South Park has returned after taking a week off for the second episode of Season 27 . The new season kicked off on July 23 with a bang. The first episode was the animated series' biggest premiere since the 90s , with a staggering 5.9 million views on Paramount+ and a 258% increase in streaming viewership after the episode aired. The show's creators, Trey Parker and Matt Stone, did not hold back. Using a real photo of Trump's face, the president was portrayed naked and in a relationship with Satan, and the episode mocked Trump's $16 million settlement with the network's parent company, Paramount Global, after suing CBS for $1.5 billion. READ MORE: Amy Bradley's brother reveals major update in the case after Netflix documentary READ MORE: New Amy Bradley leads emerge following Netflix documentary 27 years later The second episode of the season, which premiered on Wednesday, August 6, centered around school counselor Mr. Mackey being fired after budget cuts. He then goes to the bank to check how much money he has, and is told he should apply to work for Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) as they give a $50,000 signing bonus - which is an actual potential offer. Mr. Mackey then watches an ad for ICE, which pokes fun at the organization itself and its intensity. "We don’t ask for experience," the narrator of the ad says, "Just show up, we don’t care if you read a book or [are] grown up, if you’re crazy or fat or lazy, we don’t care at all.” It also adds the tagline, "If you need a job it’s a job to have.” Mr. Mackey joins and is shown an introduction video featuring the Head of Homeland Security, Kristi Noem - who South Park also pokes fun at by making her shoot and kill a dog every time she sees one - a reference to when the actual Kristi shot and killed her own dog. This isn't the first time that South Park poked fun at the Trump administration. The first episode of the season featured an AI-generated PSA where Trump strips down naked in the desert. The public service announcement refers to a demand Trump made in his lawsuit against CBS, and was marked 1 of 50, insinuating that there will be more to come as new episodes air. New episodes of South Park air Wednesdays at 10 PM EST on Comedy Central and are available to stream the following day on Paramount+.
